3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The sun was just beginning to rise as Lucian, Petr and I gathered in my office to discuss the fallout of the Benfi Festival.

4.speaker: Lucian Galade
4.text: “The news is about to break, even as we speak. We must act swiftly to protect the administration.”

9.speaker: Lucian Galade
9.text: “The most important thing is the narrative. We need to regain control of it."

10.speaker: Petr Vectern
10.text: "He also has incredible influence over the USP's conservative wing, including our MP's. We've got to act before he rallies the others against you.”

11.speaker: Lucian Galade
11.text: “At the same time, you must not apologize yourself. Insulting the First Lady is an act that should not go unpunished.”

12.speaker: Player
12.text: "You've got that right. How dare he insult my wife!”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “We could talk with him. Try to defuse the situation."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “He and his conservative cronies won't be able to stand up to the full force of our administration.”

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: “Exactly. A show of force could weaken his position.”

16.speaker: Petr Vectern
16.text: “It was unacceptable. Monica didn't deserve that.”

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: “Engaging in talks has a chance of backfiring, but it could be the simplest solution.”

18.speaker: Lucian Galade
18.text: “Perhaps she was allowed a little too much autonomy with her speech.”

19.speaker: Petr Vectern
19.text: "He acted like an ass, too. Maybe you can both come out of this looking good.”

20.speaker: Petr Vectern
20.text: “Maybe. Or just get him to dig in harder.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “We will request a formal apology from Curtan.”

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “I'm going to call Marcel Koronti. We have our deal -- let's put it to use."

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “Our deal with Marcel Koronti might be a solution.”

28.speaker: Lucian Galade
28.text: “That would be the most ideal option.”

29.speaker: Petr Vectern
29.text: "I still don't trust that man further than I could throw him. But he might prove useful in this case.”

30.speaker: Lucian Galade
30.text: “I don't expect much compliance after you forcefully removed him from the venue.”

31.speaker: Lucian Galade
31.text: "Excellent choice. With his influence on the media, this could be contained fairly easily.”

32.speaker: Marcel Koronti
32.text: “I was wondering when you would call.”

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: Petr left the room and came back with Livia. She had on a short dress and dark eyeliner -- clearly she'd been counting on me being away at the festival for longer. Still, her demeanor was nothing but professional.

34.speaker: Petr Vectern
34.text: “Maybe he's had time to cool off. I'll ask Livia to get him on the line."

35.speaker: Petr Vectern
35.text: "I'm still skeptical about this. But fine. I'll fetch Livia.”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “You seem to have forgotten how to greet people with respect.”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “Curtan. I am calling to extend the olive branch.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “You insulted my wife. Would you have acted differently if the roles were reversed?”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “It was a mistake. A grave one at that.”

44.speaker: Curtan Leste
44.text: “At the very least, you have the courage to accept that it was.”

45.speaker: Curtan Leste
45.text: “She insulted our culture and heritage. I only protected our values.”

46.speaker: Curtan Leste
46.text: “Wrong decision. I am disappointed, Mr. President.”

47.speaker: Player
47.text: “Let's put all of this behind us.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “Do you want a solution or not?”

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: He paused. The ball was in my court.

51.speaker: Curtan Leste
51.text: “Let's see how you like the press hearing about the loss of Anrica to the National Front.”

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “You just made a very powerful enemy.”

54.speaker: Curtan Leste
54.text: “You seem to be surrounded by more and more enemies these days, Mr. President.”

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Curtan Leste hung up the phone.

57.speaker: Petr Vectern
57.text: “That's going to have consequences. Is there anything else we can do?”

58.speaker: Lucian Galade
58.text: “That went worse than expected. We've lost the chance to control the narrative, and we've lost a city to another party.”

62.speaker: Lucian Galade
62.text: “That went far better than expected. We have both our apology and a chance to change the narrative."

63.speaker: Petr Vectern
63.text: “I can't believe you agreed to keep Monica out of politics. She won't take that well.”

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: Lucian departed, which left me and Petr in the room.

65.speaker: Lucian Galade
65.text: “I'll start working on our official response to his apology, to paint us in the best light possible.”

67.speaker: Marcel Koronti
67.text: “We're running out of time for pleasantries, aren't we, Mr. President?”

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “Think about this, Marcel. You don't want me on the other side of the fence.”

69.speaker: Marcel Koronti
69.text: “I've just seen the proofs for Sordland Today. It seems your incident with poor Mayor Leste is about to make headlines.”

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “We had a deal. I hope you have not forgotten.”

72.speaker: Marcel Koronti
72.text: “I know I don't. We have a deal. after all."

73.speaker: Marcel Koronti
73.text: “Deyr Journal, The Radical, Holsord Post and Lachaven Times are all prepared to print the story on the front page.”

74.speaker: Marcel Koronti
74.text: “Of course not. Mutual respect between partners is a must.”

75.speaker: Marcel Koronti
75.text: “I take it that you want this contained, if not completely gone?”

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “I only want to minimize the damage. The less prominent the story, the better.”

78.speaker: Marcel Koronti
78.text: “That's certainly within the realm of possibility. I can have you banished to the back pages in the next hour.”

79.speaker: Marcel Koronti
79.text: “Alas, the event is too newsworthy to receive no coverage. But I can have you banished to the back pages in the next hour."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “Do you think this could blow out of proportion?”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “And what would you want from me in return?”

85.speaker: Marcel Koronti
85.text: "Oh, we'll worry about that when the time comes.”

86.speaker: Marcel Koronti
86.text: “I'm not a Saint, Mr. President. I can not perform miracles. I too have my limits.”

87.speaker: Marcel Koronti
87.text: “A president replacing an invited speaker with his own wife, then forcing him out of the ceremony itself? It might go international."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “If this... partnership comes to light, it would be an even bigger scandal.”

92.speaker: Marcel Koronti
92.text: “So, do you want me to get to work?”

94.speaker: Petr Vectern
94.text: “Time to go into full damage control. This ought to end well.”

95.speaker: Lucian Galade
95.text: “I know Mr. Koronti may have dubious intentions, but it's going to be difficult to contain this media backlash on our own.”

96.speaker: Marcel Koronti
96.text: “Well in that case, I have no reason to be talking to you right now.”

99.speaker: Marcel Koronti
99.text: "After that, making the necessary changes to my own publication should be no trouble at all."

100.speaker: Marcel Koronti
100.text: “Perfect. I'll call my contacts at the other papers first -- I should be able to persuade them to downplay the situation.”

101.speaker: Marcel Koronti
101.text: “Don't you worry. Until next time, Mr. President.”

105.speaker: Petr Vectern
105.text: “I'm surprised he was so enthusiastic about it. But either way, he just made our lives easier.”

106.speaker: Lucian Galade
106.text: “I knew this partnership was the right decision. Mr. Koronti should be able to keep the incident under control.”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “Any plans for the holiday next month?”

108.speaker: Player
108.text: “How are things between you and Evelyn?”

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “How are the upcoming trade deals for Agnolia and Wehlen coming along?”

112.speaker: Petr Vectern
112.text: “As well as expected. They had their own concerns, but they'll fall in line."

113.speaker: Petr Vectern
113.text: “It's been a while since we had a drink or two together.”

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “Yes, it's been far too long. Shall we?”

117.speaker: Petr Vectern
117.text: “Right now Leste looks like the victim -- harangued for defending Sordland's precious cultural values until he had no choice but to leave."

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: “If Sordland Today paints you in a favorable light, other publications are bound to follow.”

120.speaker: Curtan Leste
120.text: “What makes you think that I will hear anything you say? You had me thrown out, for God's sake!”

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: At that very moment, the phone began to ring. The news was out.

122.speaker: Livia Suno
122.text: “I'll let you know once I have him on the line.”

123.speaker: Livia Suno
123.text: “Mr. Vectern told me what happened. Should I connect you with the mayor directly?”

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: Curtan had definitely not cooled off. I did not like his tone at all.

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: Livia left the room to arrange the call. A few minutes later, the phone line lit up.

129.speaker: Livia Suno
129.text: “I hope you won't make any compromises with Mr. Leste. He behaved like a pig at the festival."

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: Marcel Koronti, the CEO of the HOS Conglomerate, was on the line.

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: Livia left the room to arrange the call. A few minutes later, the telephone lit up.

132.speaker: Livia Suno
132.text: “To be honest, though, I think you should keep this deal in your pocket until you have a scandal worth covering up. Leste was completely in the wrong here."

133.speaker: Livia Suno
133.text: “I'll let you know once I have him on the line.”

134.speaker: Livia Suno
134.text: “Mr. Vectern told me what happened. Should I connect you to Mr. Koronti directly?"

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: Petr left the room and came back with my secretary. She had on a short dress and dark eyeliner -- clearly she'd been counting on me being away at the festival for longer. Still, her demeanor was nothing but professional.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: Mayor Curtan Leste's untimely departure was bound to reflect badly on me. The only question was how much damage the incident would cause.

140.speaker: Player
140.text: “I demand a public and formal apology for your behavior at the festival."

141.speaker: Curtan Leste
141.text: “Is that so? You've got some nerve.”

142.speaker: Curtan Leste
142.text: “Why would I possibly apologize to you? You had me thrown out, for God's sake!”

145.speaker: Curtan Leste
145.text: “The First Lady won't be allowed to meddle in politics from now on. No meetings. No advocating for her little causes. And certainly no speeches."

146.speaker: Curtan Leste
146.text: “Should you fail to keep her from doing so, you can say your goodbyes to Anrica."

147.speaker: Curtan Leste
147.text: "On the other hand, if you do this, I will issue a full apology and your party will retain my support."

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “You leave me no choice. I'll tell Monica she's out of politics."

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “I refuse. You are the one who is in the wrong. I won't punish her for your crimes.”

152.speaker: Curtan Leste
152.text: “I'm glad that we came to terms.”

153.speaker: Curtan Leste
153.text: “I will announce my public apology to the press immediately.”

159.speaker: Marcel Koronti
159.text: “Apologies for my behaviour, Mr. President, but we both know that time is of the essence.”

160.speaker: Marcel Koronti
160.text: “But in times like these, I'm your personal lord and savior. You know that. Otherwise you wouldn't have called.”

161.speaker: Marcel Koronti
161.text: “That is a big *if*, Mr. President, compared to what is happening *now*.”

162.speaker: Marcel Koronti
162.text: “But it is your decision. So what will it be?”

164.speaker: Player
164.text: “I changed my mind. It's too risky.”

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: He leaned back in his chair.

166.speaker: Player
166.text: “For God's sake, Petr, it's six in the morning!”

168.speaker: Petr Vectern
168.text: “Right now Leste looks like the victim, thrown out of the festival for defending Sordland's precious cultural values.”

172.speaker: Lucian Galade
172.text: "Considering he opted to leave the venue rather than deliver an apology last night, I would hardly expect one from him now."

182.speaker: Curtan Leste
182.text: “What makes you think that I will hear anything you say? You humiliated me in front of my entire home city!"

183.speaker: Curtan Leste
183.text: “Why would I possibly apologize to you? You humiliated me in front of my entire home city!"

186.speaker: Lucian Galade
186.text: "Talk to Koronti, Mr. President. Unless you'd rather take advice from someone in a conical brassiere.”

187.speaker: Lucian Galade
187.text: "A compromise may be necessary, Mr. President. Unless you'd rather take advice from someone in a conical brassiere.”

189.speaker: Lucian Galade
189.text: “That does not look like it went good.”

190.speaker: Petr Vectern
190.text: “Is there anything else we can do?”

194.speaker: Lucian Galade
194.text: “We could give a call to Mr. Koronti.”

199.speaker: Player
199.text: “Let's just talk to him. He can't stay angry forever.”

200.speaker: Lucian Galade
200.text: "Considering he opted to leave the venue rather than deliver an apology last night, I would hardly expect anything from him now."

204.speaker: Lucian Galade
204.text: “I don't expect much compliance after you forcefully removed him from the venue.”
